This chunk is about:
- People: Neil B. Shulman, Michael Caton-Jones, Jeffrey Price, Peter S. Seaman, Dallas Hall, Elijah Saunders
- Organizations: International Society on Hypertension in Blacks
- Products: Doc Hollywood, What?, Ethnicity & Disease
- Topics: hypertension among African Americans, minority health

Facts:
- In 1986, physicians Dallas Hall, Neil B. Shulman, and Elijah Saunders founded the International Society on Hypertension in Blacks in response to concern about high rates of hypertension among African Americans.
- In 1991, the film Doc Hollywood was released as an American romantic comedy directed by Michael Caton-Jones and written by Jeffrey Price and Peter S. Seaman.
- In 1991, Doc Hollywood was based on Neil B. Shulman's book What?, and Neil B. Shulman was an associate producer of the film.
- In 1991, Ethnicity & Disease was established as the official journal of the International Society on Hypertension in Blacks and is published by that society.
- By 2006, the International Society on Hypertension in Blacks had broadened its scope from reducing hypertension among African Americans to improving the health of minority populations worldwide.
